headline_marked: [[Mymensingh hospital fire]] sparks panic; casualty count disputed, probe launched
headline: Mymensingh hospital fire sparks panic; casualty count disputed, probe launched
summary: A fire at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital caused panic among patients and relatives. Initial reports of six stampede deaths were later refuted by officials, who confirmed two natural deaths and are investigating others.
details: A fire erupted on the eighth floor of the new building at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital on Monday afternoon, around 5:30 PM. The news of the fire quickly spread, causing widespread panic among patients and their relatives, who began rushing to evacuate.

Initial police reports indicated six deaths due to stampede during the evacuation. However, the Divisional Commissioner later clarified that this information was incorrect, stating that two of the reported deaths were from natural causes, one person was found alive, and the cause of death for two others remains unclear. He denied any deaths occurred due to stampede.

Allegations have surfaced that only one of the four staircases in the building was open during the emergency, contributing to the chaos. The ongoing investigation will examine why most stairways were closed or unusable at the time of the fire and if any irregularities occurred.

Fire service personnel, with four units, swiftly responded to the scene and brought the blaze under control. Preliminary investigations suggest the fire originated from an electrical short circuit in the controller machine connected to the lift control room, likely due to excessive heat.

A five-member investigation committee has been formed by the hospital authority to ascertain the exact cause of the incident, assess the overall situation during the fire, and determine the accurate number and cause of any casualties.

headline: ICT verdict today for Obaidul Quader and six others in crimes against humanity case
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 is set to deliver its judgment in a case concerning atrocities during the July Uprising in 2024. All seven accused, including former minister Obaidul Quader, are currently absconding.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 is scheduled to deliver its verdict today for Obaidul Quader and six others in a crimes against humanity case. The charges relate to alleged atrocities committed during the July Uprising in 2024.
After approximately eight months of trial, the tribunal announced yesterday that the judgment would be delivered today. All seven accused, including Quader, are currently absconding.

Quader, who served as a minister four times and is the Awami League general secretary for three consecutive terms, faces a verdict that could determine his fate. The other accused include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AFM Bahauddin Nasim, Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, Moinul Hossain Nikhil, Saddam Hussain, and Sheikh Wali Asif Enan.

According to the prosecution, Quader, in his capacity as AL general secretary and a cabinet minister, allegedly exercised command and control over law enforcement agencies and armed cadres. These groups reportedly suppressed the quota reform movement that began on July 1, 2024.

The prosecution further alleges that more than 1,400 protesters were killed and over 25,000 seriously injured. These widespread, systematic, and targeted attacks on the civilian population were allegedly carried out with the accused’s knowledge and involvement.
Nasim is accused of helping organize and facilitate the party’s response, while Arafat allegedly played a role in controlling media and suppressing reports of killings and violence.

Parash and Nikhil are accused of mobilizing Jubo League activists, with Nikhil specifically alleged to have opened fire on protesters. BCL leaders Saddam and Enan are accused of assembling armed cadres and coordinating attacks.

The investigation commenced on June 18, 2025, and the report was submitted to the prosecution on December 7. The tribunal took cognisance of the charges on December 18 and framed them on January 22, 2026.
The trial began on February 17, with 29 prosecution witnesses testifying. Both prosecution and defence completed their closing arguments over nine working days, from August 4 to 17.
